summary: The screened 2026-09-11 arXiv slice contains one strong direct heavy-ion phenomenology contribution on efficient jet-wake medium response, a useful small-system non-flow caution, a compact light-nuclei/hypernuclei proceedings synthesis, and several high-value statistical or AI/ML methods with credible HEP/nuclear transfer. Recurring themes are jet-induced hydrodynamic wakes, multiplicity-biased non-flow, coalescence and feed-down, physics-guided Gaussian-process priors, nuisance-parameter-aware measurement combinations, distribution-shift quantification, detector-defined dataset contamination, and operations drift diagnosis.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2609.10679 is the strongest direct heavy-ion paper: it introduces an Efficient Wake procedure for jet-induced hydrodynamic response, benchmarks it against full 3+1D nonlinear hydrodynamics, and reports very large speedups suitable for Monte Carlo jet phenomenology.

papers.title: Computationally Efficient Description of Medium Response to Jets in Heavy Ion Collisions
papers.short_authors: Jorge Casalderrey-Solana, Jose Guilherme Milhano, Daniel Pablos, Krishna Rajagopal, Xiaojun Yao
papers.abstract: The paper develops an Efficient Wake procedure for jet-induced hydrodynamic response using reusable linearized-hydrodynamic templates mapped onto freezeout with longitudinal expansion and radial-flow effects, benchmarked against full nonlinear 3+1D hydrodynamics.

papers.title: Study of the multiplicity dependence of non-flow correlations in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=200 GeV using PYTHIA
papers.abstract: Using PYTHIA at RHIC energy, the authors test whether non-flow correlations can be transferred from low to high multiplicity and find that multiplicity selections bias jet dynamics and non-flow scaling.

papers.title: Production of Light Nuclei and Hypernuclei in Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: A proceedings review of STAR and ALICE light-nucleus and hypernucleus yields, femtoscopy, and flow, emphasizing coalescence, feed-down, nuclear structure, and production chronology.

papers.title: Collinear fragmentation of pseudoscalar quarkonia from NLO NRQCD
papers.abstract: The paper announces NRFF1.0 collinear fragmentation functions for pseudoscalar quarkonia using NLO NRQCD inputs and heavy-flavor evolution, with possible use as a quarkonium-in-jet baseline for medium studies.

papers.title: Nuclear-physics-guided Gaussian Processes
papers.short_authors: Javier Rozalen Sarmiento, Hristijan Kochankovski, Arnau Rios, Angels Ramos
papers.abstract: Physics-motivated mean functions and kernels are encoded in Gaussian-process regression for nuclear phase shifts, mass excesses, and finite-temperature dense-matter equations of state, improving interpolation, calibration, and extrapolation over agnostic priors.

papers.title: Combinations of measurements that are simultaneous fits of parameters of interest and systematic uncertainties using the BLUE method
papers.short_authors: Tomas Dado, Mark Owen, Michele Pinamonti
papers.abstract: The authors extend BLUE combinations to fitted nuisance parameters as well as parameters of interest, validate uncertainty behavior with pseudo-experiments, and provide an open-source implementation.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Drift Diagnosis for Laser-Plasma Accelerator Operations
papers.short_authors: Ou Labun, Calin Hojbota, Mara Klebonas, Mike Downer, Rafal Zgadzaj, Phil Franke, Lance Labun
papers.abstract: A latent state-space model and extended Kalman filter infer effective laser-plasma variables from routine diagnostics in synthetic sessions, separating emission and transition models for drift attribution.

papers.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts
papers.abstract: The paper introduces estimable covariate and concept shift measures based on entropic optimal transport, derives generalization bounds and concentration guarantees, and proposes the DataShifts algorithm.

papers.title: Prevalence Determines Precision: Silent Contamination in Detector-Defined Datasets
papers.short_authors: Jia Huang, Yankai Wan, Yangjun Ou
papers.abstract: The paper shows that detector- or heuristic-defined dataset precision depends strongly on true-positive prevalence, with contamination able to inherit detector-shaped structure rather than behave as additive noise.

cautions.title: Bayesian Superiority in On/Off analysis
cautions.abstract: The paper compares Bayesian non-informative-prior criteria with Li-Ma for On/Off counting problems and reports lower Type I and Type II error rates in simulations, including overdispersed backgrounds.
